Subject: Renewal: Request for priority support + latency SLO for Q2 expansion

Hi Soojin,

Hope you’re well. We’re planning a material expansion of LumenTech’s usage of the Redwood API starting in early Q2 — roughly 3x requests/day and a bigger percent of real-time inference for customer-facing flows. Given the higher business impact, procurement wants us on a premium support tier with stronger latency SLOs and a predictable capacity plan before the renewal on Mar 1.

Specifically, we’d like:
- 99.95% availability for our dedicated endpoint
- p95 latency target <= 300ms (production traffic, 512 tokens)
- 24/7 P1 on-call with a 30 min response SLA
- Burst capacity reserve for occasional traffic spikes (up to 2x baseline)

Can Redwood share a written addendum (SLA + support runbook + pricing delta) and a DocuSign link that procurement can route in the next two weeks? Our legal/procurement timeline is tight — they need something by 2/2 to keep the March 1 renewal on schedule.

Thanks,
Eva
Eva Morales
Head of Platform Operations

Thanks — I sketched numbers and an operational approach. High level:

1) SLA & SLOs (measurement on prod endpoint, 30d rolling window):
   - Availability: 99.95% uptime for their dedicated endpoint
   - Latency (512 token baseline): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 800ms
   - Error rate cap: <= 0.2% 5xx
   - Credits: standard crediting on missed SLOs (service credit % proportional to window missed)

2) Capacity & burst model:
   - Committed baseline: size for 1.25x their Q1 average (buffer for steady growth)
   - Burst reserve: configurable burst pool that can scale to 2x baseline for short windows (up to 30m sustained)
   - If bursts exceed 2x or are sustained >30m, we apply throttling rules with pre-notification and automatic fallback to a compatible lower-cost model variant

3) Support & on-call:
   - 24/7 P1 on-call with 30-minute response and 4-hour remediation SLA (ops-led)
   - Priority escalation path: primary on-call -> engineering lead -> throughput SRE manager -> CS executive (contact list included)
   - Quarterly operational review and a runbook stored in a shared Drive

4) Pricing (monthly):
   - Committed monthly fee: $28,000 (covers baseline up to committed units)
   - Burst buffer add-on: $6,000/month for up to 2x burst reserve (pre-provisioned capacity)
   - Overages above committed+burst: metered at $0.015 per token-equivalent
   - One-time onboarding & runbook creation: $7,500 (waived if contract signed by 2029-02-02)

5) Short-term credit to close the renewal: 25% credit on month 1 if signed by 2029-02-02

I attached a short SLA addendum with the exact SLO language. Grace — can you attach the runbook and confirm the on-call roster commitment? Marissa — confirm Dedicated pool availability for 2x burst in their region (us-west).

Attachment: Proposed_SLA_Addendum_draft.pdf

- Rishi
